plan._about: 10th National Socio-Economic Development Plan 2026-2030 (NSEDP). op '>=' = at least, '<=' = at most. 'actual' says which number is compared (see js/pages/eco-plan.js): the newest one the app has, an automatic series or a hand-read fact. Only a number from inside 'period' gets a status; an earlier one is the baseline. 'checked' = the day the targets were last read in the two KPL articles (all 14 targets and the project numbers matched).

facts._about: Numbers quoted from the reports; the sentences are in i18n (inv_debt_*, inv_drivers_*, inv_fdi_where_*, inv_infl_why_*), the numbers here. Re-read on 2026-10-02 in the June 2026 edition of the World Bank's Lao Economic Monitor (wb_lem_2606): debt level, deferrals, debt service, reserves, growth, foreign investment and inflation now quote that edition; the peak of 2022, the share of EDL, the creditor shares, the bond and the decree are from the December 2025 edition (wb_lem). Debt service: the report gives the same US$1.5 billion a year for 2026-2030 twice - in its debt chapter as 'external debt service ... excluding deferrals', in its outlook as 'on external and domestic debt'. The debt chapter's wording is used (scope: external): it fits the report's other numbers (about US$2 billion in 2026; 13 percent of GDP in 2026, which is a different measure and therefore a fact of its own, debt_service_year). debt_mof = the Ministry of Finance's own count (2025 Public Debt Bulletin, as quoted in the report): 84% of GDP at the end of 2025; the World Bank's 87.1% adds deferred interest, currency swaps and expenditure arrears. reserves_wb: 'months' = months of imports of goods and services (World Bank), 'months_bol' = the Bank of the Lao PDR's own count for the same US$4.3 billion (footnote 6 of the report: without the goods imports of foreign businesses that earn export revenues or bring in their own capital).

debt_wb._about: Public and publicly guaranteed debt in % of GDP as the World Bank counts it (with expenditure arrears and swaps), by year, for the second line of the debt chart. 2022 and 2023: table 'selected indicators' on page 16 of the December 2025 report (wb_lem; the same report's text rounds the 2022 peak to 130, the table prints 131). 2024 to 2028: table 3 of the June 2026 report (wb_lem_2606); 2025 is an estimate, the years from first_forecast on are forecasts. 2024 = 94 in both editions. scripts/check-data.js compares these values with the copies in debt_peak and policy (level, outlook). Read 2026-10-04.

gold._about: How pure the two gold bars are whose prices the site compares (fineness as a share: 99.99% = 0.9999). scripts/build-summary.js reads these two numbers for the like-for-like premium - fine gold in an LBB bar against fine gold in a Thai bar, gram for gram (audit 2026-10-02, P2-1). LBB: the panel with its rates is headed 'LBB Gold Bar 99.99% International Standard' (Lao: 'ຄຳແທ່ງ LBB ມາດຕະຖານສາກົນ 999.9%'); read in the script of laobullionbank.com on 2026-10-04. Thailand: the association's bar price is the price of gold of 96.5%, per baht-weight of 15.244 g.

rubber._about: Prices of rubber INSIDE Laos that could be found online (all channels re-checked 2026-10-01: official sites, news, social media, international datasets). No daily or provincial series is published. official_yearly = item 204 'ຢາງພາລາ (ລາຄານ້ຳຢາງດິບ)' of the ministry's table, kip per tonne, national average (its 5 values sit under the 2019-2023 columns). reports = single numbers quoted in news; 'period' is what the number refers to.

production_basis._about: How the FAO counts rubber production (for the note that explains why more rubber is recorded as sold abroad than as produced): the FAO's primary crop is the latex 'concentrated, stabilized and dried' - dry rubber - while customs record the weight of the goods as shipped. Read 2026-10-04.

provinces._about: Rubber area by province, hectares: [province, planted, tapped]. The newest table by province that is published (page 18 of the report; NAFRI 2018, unpublished data). Houaphan and Xiengkhouang have no 2018 figure. The source prints the tapped area of Xaisomboun as '53,95'; 5,395 is what makes the printed total (121,394) add up. The planted areas add up to 257,887, the printed total is 258,446.

land._about: Official ASSESSED land prices exist per province (base for land tax and fees, not market prices): data/land.json lists the decisions found in the Lao Official Gazette. Vientiane Capital's decision is not in the Gazette list; a Thai translation of its table was published by ThaiPublica (official_extra). No open data of real sale prices was found (re-checked 2026-10-01); listing sites show ASKING prices only, mostly Vientiane Capital.

vientiane._about: Vientiane Capital, Decision 142 of 26 Feb 2024: official assessed land prices, LAK per square metre, by road class. Summary made from the 976 price lines of the Thai translation published by ThaiPublica (computed 2026-10-01): per district [lowest, middle (median of the price lines), highest]. 'villages' = number of villages named in the district's heading. The full table by village is in the linked PDF and is NOT copied here (it is the publisher's translation); 'page' = the page of that PDF (62 pages) on which the district's heading stands, so the page can send the reader straight there.

population._about: Facts for the Population tab that no API provides. Sentences are in i18n (pop_*). household = average number of people per household, read on 2026-10-03 in the United Nations' database (rows 'Lao People's Dem. Republic': MICS 2017 = 4.7, of which 1 person 3.2% and 6 or more 29.4% of households; Demographic Yearbook / census 2015 = 5.3). The World Bank's API has no household size; a newer survey (LSIS III) is not in the 2022 edition of the database.

policy._about: What the State decided and what follows from it, for the Policy tab. One entry = one fact read in its source; the sentences are in i18n (pol_<area>_<id>), the numbers here. 'affects' = which numbers on the site the area moves; 'tab' = where to look at the effect. The two money items 'rate' and 'reserve' are the fallback: the page shows data/bol-policy.json (read from the central bank's site every week) when that file is there. 'read' = the edition of the World Bank's Lao Economic Monitor these facts were read from: data/report-watch.json (weekly) tells the page when a newer edition is out. An item can name more sources in 'sources'. Re-checked against the primary sources on 2026-10-02: the fuel excise cut is now quoted from the ministry's own notice (regular petrol 25% -> 15%; the World Bank's report says 30% -> 15% and premium 40% -> 15%), and the partial return of the tax on 25 June 2026 was added.

wages._about: Statutory minimum wages in force, read by hand from each government's notice (or from the news agency that reports it), for the Wages tab: the 11 members of ASEAN, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, the United States, Israel. steps = [day it starts, amount, (monthly amount named by the law itself)] in the country's currency per 'per' (hour | day | month); the page uses the last step whose day has come and names the next one. Without a monthly amount from the law, the page multiplies: an hour x 'hours_per_month' (40 hours x 52 weeks / 12 - the ILO's own conversion), a day x 'days_per_month'. Australia's monthly amount = its weekly amount (A$1,004.90 for 38 hours) x 52 / 12. kind: national = one rate for the whole country; top = the highest regional rate (the capital or the richest region), 'low' = the lowest regional rate when the same notice names it; sector = only the sectors named in the law; average = Japan publishes the weighted average of its 47 prefectures; none = no general minimum wage. Notes per country are in i18n (wg_note_<iso>); numbers named in a note are fields of the country here (low, prev, lqs, proposal, hours, weekly). thailand = the daily rates of Notification No. 14 in the industrial provinces, the provinces along the Lao border, and the lowest rate.
